regime_context: The detector shows a broad (9/16 eligible) but non-directional rotation with Gold Miners leading (score 1.8, durability 0.66, breadth 0.933) over Silver & Royalties (1.627). This is an attention/focus lens, not an alpha signal; the validated edge is only drawdown control via the absolute-trend gate, which on this market's history does help (gate_helps=true). I offer lean, low-conviction leans only where the trend gate plus breadth support staying power.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Silver & Royalties closes the gap with Gold Miners in the rotation margin (currently 0.173). A confirmed handoff would be visible if Silver & Royalties' score exceeds Gold Miners' for 5 consecutive sessions while both remain eligible; if that condition does not occur, the watch simply lapses at the next state date.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners lead the rotation with the highest score (1.8), a strong durability bar (0.66), and high breadth (0.933), suggesting leadership is cohesive rather than a single-name spike. The absolute-trend gate marks it eligible, and crowding is not extreme (z=0.54), so the only validated risk-control leg does not object to holding it. This is a modest stay-with-the-trend lean, not a return forecast.
evidence: eligible=true via the absolute-trend gate (the one validated leg)
theses.dissent: Gold miners are famously reflexive to real rates and the macro backdrop here is dominated by AI/tech and geopolitics headlines, not a fresh gold-specific driver; the rank itself has ~0 forward IC, so the leadership could simply be attention without follow-through.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms the S&P/TSX by more than 5% over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the nearest challenger (score 1.627) to Gold Miners, with similarly high breadth (0.917) and an eligible trend gate. It is effectively a satellite of the same precious-metals leadership theme; the rotation radar shows a narrow margin (0.173) to the leader, suggesting the theme is intact, not breaking down. Lean here is a same-theme expression, not a distinct view.
theses.dissent: Silver is higher-beta than gold and can fall harder in a risk-off tape; the silver-specific industrial component ties it to manufacturing demand that the state does not reveal, adding a driver this desk cannot verify from the given state.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO (the proxy) drops below the S&P/TSX by 5% cumulative before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the strongest eligible non-materials theme (score 0.75) and the only one tagged 'trend' in the detector, with a healthy durability bar of 0.66. In a market where the only validated edge is the absolute-trend gate, a trend-healthy eligible theme with neutral crowding (z=0.56) is the kind of name that avoids shake-outs. Breadth is modest (0.429), so this is a slow, defensive lean rather than a momentum call.
theses.dissent: Canadian banks are rate-sensitive and the macro backdrop of dominant AI/tech and geopolitics headlines offers no fundamental tailwind for domestic financials; the breadth of 0.429 means leadership is not broad, so the rank may reflect a handful of large caps rather than a genuine sector move.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO falls below its own 40-day moving average and stays there for 5 consecutive sessions before the check-by date
